quotes.speaker: Maxime Aubin
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's focus on simplifying his isolation game
quotes.excerpt: he wants to do less and do it better and to repeat the same movements again and again
quotes.quote: I was asking Victor Wembanyama about his isolation game. He said during media day that he wanted to really improve his isolation game. I asked him after five games how he feels about it, is he improving, in what area? He was basically trying to say that he is trying to simplify his game. This is still a work in progress as we can see. The whole point was for him to say that he wants to do less and do it better and to repeat the same movements again and again. Once again, he is not there yet. I think that is the craziest part about Wembanyama, he can average 35, 10 rebounds and four blocks, and you watch his offensive game and you are like, it is a mess, we do not understand what is going on.
quotes.social_post: Victor Wembanyama is focusing on simplifying his isolation game. Maxime Aubin notes that despite his massive stats, Wembanyama is working to do less and do it better by repeating the same movements.

structured.context: Maxime Aubin discusses Victor Wembanyama's efforts to simplify his isolation game after observing his performance early in the season.

quotes.speaker: Maxime Aubin
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's reaction to criticism following the finals
quotes.excerpt: this is still something that hurts him, what happened in the finals
quotes.quote: After the finals, with all the criticism he had, I was really hopeful I could try to talk to him to get him one-on-one, like a lot of other people. Let's say he was very quiet. I talked to his people, to his agents, and they said basically he does not want to talk about the finals. From what I understand now, this is still something that hurts him, what happened in the finals. He does not really want to talk about it yet. He wants to answer on the court and he wants to make the right choices this time and go all the way to the finals and this time to win it.
quotes.social_post: Victor Wembanyama is still processing the loss in the NBA finals. According to Maxime Aubin, Wembanyama is declining interviews about the series because it still hurts and he wants to answer on the court.

structured.context: Maxime Aubin explains that Victor Wembanyama is avoiding public discussion regarding the previous season's finals loss while focusing on future success.

quotes.speaker: Maxime Aubin
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's desire to represent the youth of France
quotes.excerpt: he feels a lot about what is happening to the young generation in France
quotes.quote: He had the short summer, the NBA finals went all the way to mid-June, then he played for the French national team this summer. What he told me recently is that he can have the FOMO a little bit of France. He wished the summer could be longer, just to spend more time there, but also to prepare better for the NBA season. Also, the whole situation in France, we have a lot of protests right now and he feels a lot about what is happening to the young generation in France. He wants to have a voice, so I think he kind of wished he was there just to be a voice for the young people of France.
quotes.social_post: Victor Wembanyama feels a sense of FOMO regarding France. He expressed a desire to be a voice for the young generation in France amidst the current social climate in the country.

structured.context: Maxime Aubin shares that Victor Wembanyama expressed a desire to spend more time in France to support the younger generation amidst current social unrest.

quotes.speaker: Maxime Aubin
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's perspective on being labeled a villain
quotes.excerpt: maybe I am the villain but I think it is a pretty good news
quotes.quote: It is a little crazy to think that he is a villain, to be honest with you. I am really trying to be objective and I have watched the finals again and again. They all play hard, they all play tough, they are rough sometimes. It went both ways for me with many players and I think Wembanyama said it for himself. He said, maybe I am the villain but I think it is a pretty good news, that means they care about me or something like that. That is how I feel about it. It is funny actually, because two days ago I have a friend who lives in New York, I used to live in New York, and every time I post something about Wembanyama and the Spurs, I get a lot of shit from Knicks fans saying Wembanyama is the worst.
quotes.social_post: Victor Wembanyama is embracing the villain label. He told Maxime Aubin that being viewed as a villain is actually good news because it means people care about him.

structured.context: Maxime Aubin reflects on the public perception of Victor Wembanyama as a villain and mentions the negative reactions from New York Knicks fans.

quotes.speaker: Maxime Aubin
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's adjustment to FIBA basketball
quotes.excerpt: he is still trying to adjust to the FIBA basketball, so there is way less space
quotes.quote: He played four games this summer. Two were just friendly games, and they were basically preparing for the World Cup qualifiers. I went to the one they played in Paris against Slovenia. Luka Doncic was not playing, unfortunately. They won against Slovenia, he had a great game. I think he is still trying to adjust to the FIBA basketball, so there is way less space. It is very interesting for him, and especially to prepare him for the NBA season because he gets beat up every time, he does not have access to the paint at all. So things that he can experience in the NBA, I think it is good for him.
quotes.social_post: Maxime Aubin says Victor Wembanyama is still adjusting to the physicality of FIBA basketball. The lack of space and constant contact in international play is providing a unique challenge for his development.

structured.context: Maxime Aubin discusses Victor Wembanyama's experience adjusting to the physical nature of FIBA basketball during his summer games.
